source_row.item_data_json: {"options":{"A":"Make seasonal influenza vaccination available at no cost because it is the vaccine specified by the Bloodborne Pathogens Standard.","B":"Make MMR vaccination available because it is the required postexposure vaccine for occupational blood exposure.","C":"Make Tdap vaccination available because it is the vaccine OSHA specifically mandates for bloodborne-pathogen exposure.","D":"Make hepatitis B vaccination available at no cost to employees with occupational exposure, subject to the standard’s stated exceptions."}}
source_row.rationale: 29 CFR 1910.1030 requires the employer to make hepatitis B vaccination available to employees with occupational exposure and to provide it at no cost. The standard includes exceptions such as prior completion of the series, demonstrated immunity, or medical contraindication.
source_row.source_detail: Paragraph 1910.1030(f): hepatitis B vaccination and no-cost requirement Source has no separate formal version identifier in the cited page metadata; live currentness and applicability rechecked 2026-08-15. source_row.stem: A healthcare employee has occupational exposure to blood or other potentially infectious material. Which vaccine must the employer make available at no cost under OSHA's Bloodborne Pathogens Standard?
